profile.reading:
The address on file for this facility, 350 Holger Way in the North San Jose district of San Jose, California, sits inside District 237, a multi-building office park developed in the late 1990s near the interchange of Highway 237 and North First Street, a corridor lined with technology-company offices and, a short distance away, some of Silicon Valley's better-known wholesale and retail data-center buildings (including the separate, unrelated multi-tenant colocation building at 400 Holger Way). The 350 Holger Way building itself is a three-story, roughly 96,500-square-foot steel-frame structure completed in 1999 and renovated in 2019. Commercial real-estate records show that KBS, an institutional office-property investor, sold the building to Thor Equities for $50.5 million in December 2020, at which point it was reported as fully leased through 2027; the brokerage records reviewed for this entry do not name the tenant or tenants occupying the space.

Dell, the operator on record for this facility, is a multinational computer-hardware and IT-services company with a substantial Northern California footprint that grew considerably after its 2016 acquisition of EMC Corporation, which itself had a long-standing Bay Area engineering and storage-systems presence. It is common, and unremarkable, for a company of Dell's size to maintain internal technical space, server rooms, lab environments, or regional IT infrastructure, inside a standard leased office building rather than in a purpose-built, publicly marketed data center; such spaces typically do not appear in commercial real-estate listings by tenant name, and none of the property records located for 350 Holger Way name Dell specifically.

No square footage of technical space, power capacity, cooling design, or redundancy tier has been published for whatever Dell facility exists at this address, and neither Dell's corporate site nor general reference sources describe this specific building. That absence is itself informative: unlike the marketed colocation and wholesale data centers nearby on Holger Way, this address reads as private, internal infrastructure serving Dell's own operations rather than a commercial facility open to outside tenants, the kind of building a large technology company operates quietly as part of its office footprint rather than promotes as a data-center product to prospective customers.

reading.body:
Dell operates a facility at 350 Holger Way in North San Jose, but publishes no power capacity, floor space, or technical specifications for this location. The company confirms ownership as of September 2026, yet the site remains opaque to public disclosure. Without published figures, this campus cannot be ranked among California's disclosed data center capacity.

California has 103 mapped data center facilities of which only 11 publish power specifications totaling 365 MW. This facility does not appear in that published set. Dell's 350 Holger Way thus contributes an unknown amount to both the state's total and Dell's own disclosed footprint.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the absence of published specifications means it cannot yet be counted. The facility exists and Dell owns it, but the binding constraint on evaluating its role in AI compute is the lack of any public statement of its power delivery, electrical infrastructure, or intended use. Until Dell publishes capacity figures, this location remains invisible to grid-constrained AI planning.
